mekki-muskil:1-1.t: His saying, Exalted is He (لإيلاف): the lām, according to al-Akhfash, is attached to (mutaʿalliq) His saying (فجعلهم كعصف), i.e. He did that to them so that Quraysh might be united; but there is remoteness in this, because of the consensus of all on the permissibility of pausing at the end of (ألم تر). And it was said: the lām is attached to an implied verb, its implied form being «اعجبوا لإيلاف قريش رحلة الشتاء والصيف وتركهم عبادة رب هذا البيت» (marvel at the uniting of Quraysh in the journey of winter and summer, and their abandoning the worship of the Lord of this House); this is the position of al-Farrāʾ. Al-Khalīl said: the lām is attached to His saying (فليعبدوا), as though He said: because Allah united Quraysh in a uniting, let them worship the Lord of this House.

mekki-muskil:2-2.t:
His saying (إيلافهم): a badal (substitute) for the first, for additional clarity, as you say «سمعت كلامك كلامك زيدا». (إيلاف) is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of a quadriliteral verb. Whoever read it «إلفهم» made it the maṣdar of a triliteral verb. Al-Farrāʾ allowed «إيلافَهم» in the accusative as a maṣdar.
His saying (رحلة الشتاء): accusative by (إيلافهم). There are two dialects in it, reported by Abū ʿUbayd: «ألِفته» and «آلفته»; and on that basis it was read (لإيلاف) and «لإلاف», from «ألف» and from «آلف». [Translator's note: the printed text has «وءلالف», evidently a corruption of the second reading.]
